title: Weekly nature
tomorrow: a crowd wept when the old book was read. why were they told to stop?

lines: BEHOLD THE FOWLS OF THE AIR.
cards: A list of what could go wrong next month can get longer every time it's read. On a mountainside, Matthew says, Jesus spoke to people worried about the basics: what shall we eat, what shall we wear.
He didn't hand them a budget. He sent them outdoors. Behold the fowls of the air, he said: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them.

teach.b: Today's question: what is time outdoors for?
Jesus goes on: Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin: and yet I say unto you, that even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
Consider asks for more than a glance: look, and keep looking. The teaching is Christian trust: creation shows the Father's care, and looking at it long enough loosens worry's grip on tomorrow.
Jesus doesn't tell the crowd to stop working.
He tells them to go and look, until worry is the size it ought to be. Now a neighbor. The Qur'an also sends its listeners outside.
In one surah it asks: will they not look at the camels, how they are made, at the sky, how it is raised, at the mountains, how they are set, at the earth, how it is spread out?
Elsewhere the Qur'an calls the heavens and the earth ayat, signs, the same word it uses for its own verses. So both read the outdoors like a page. And an honest difference, in these two passages.
Jesus points to birds and flowers to teach trust in the Father's care. Surah 88 points to camel, sky and mountain as signs that lead the mind to their Maker.
Same looking, a different lesson drawn from it.
Two hours outdoors a week is long enough to do either.

how: Christians read Jesus' words on the birds and the lilies in the Sermon on the Mount as teaching about trust in God's care; Muslims read the Qur'an's call to look at the camel, sky, mountains and earth as reflection on God's signs.

o: a hike counted as worship instead of prayer
a weekly workout done outside to burn more energy
two hours outside each week, spent really looking

games.q: the lilies and the signs: tap the pairs.
p: they sow not, yet are fed
Solomon was not arrayed like these
the camel, the sky, the mountains
signs that lead to their Maker

s: Jesus told the worried crowd to stop working and do nothing
he pointed to birds and lilies to loosen worry, not to forbid work.
the Qur'an uses one word for its verses and for signs in nature
ayat: the same word for both.
Jesus and the Qur'an teach exactly the same lesson from nature
both send people to look. in these passages Jesus draws trust in God's care; surah 88 draws signs that lead to their Maker.

games.q: your friend says hiking is her religion and the old books just say 'nature is God.' how would you put the two sources fairly?
o: both send people outside to look: Jesus to trust, the Qur'an to see God's signs.
both say nature and God are the same thing, so any hike is worship.
both say time outdoors can stand in for gathering to pray.
games.why: Jesus says consider the lilies, because the Father cares for them; the Qur'an calls the camel and the sky ayat, signs of their Maker. Shared looking, honest difference, and neither says nature is God.

practice: Step outside, or open a window. Find one living thing, a bird, a tree, a weed in a crack, and keep your eyes on it the whole time, the way you'd read a page slowly.
When the bell rings, choose the day this week for your two hours outdoors.

wordCard.voice: Weekly nature: two hours outdoors each week, spent considering, the way Jesus sent a worried crowd to the lilies and the Qur'an points to its signs.

orig.note: Arabic: signs, also the word for the Qur'an's verses.

carryVoice: Your line: outdoors, where the lilies and the signs are waiting to be read. Go gently.
